threat: Exfiltrate Guest and Employee Records from Hotel Management Platforms
threat_description: Adversaries target the rich repositories of personal data hospitality operators centralize — guest profiles, reservation histories, payment credentials, loyalty account records, employee PII, and corporate client information. Hotels are high-value targets: they hold travel patterns, payment cards, passport scans, and stay preferences for millions of guests across shared PMS, CRS, and SaaS platforms. A single breach of a shared management platform propagates exfiltration across every property on that system. The attacker does not need to compromise the guest — they compromise the infrastructure the guest trusted.

motives.motive: Exfiltrate guest personal and payment data from centralized hotel management platforms for identity theft, fraud, or resale

components.name: Property Management System (PMS)
components.description: The central operational platform managing guest check-ins, reservations, billing, and room assignments across hotel properties — Opera, Mews, Cloudbeds, Oracle Hospitality. Contains the most comprehensive guest data store in the hotel ecosystem.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hard-coded credentials embedded in PMS installations cannot be rotated or revoked - any attacker who recovers them from a binary, config file or vendor documentation gains permanent access to guest records, billing histories and room assignment data across every property running the affected version.

PMS administrative accounts protected by a password alone give credential stuffing, phishing and infostealer campaigns a single-step path to the full guest database - there is no second factor between a leaked password and bulk export of guest profiles, passport scans and stay histories.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SQL injection in PMS query interfaces allows attackers to bypass application-layer access controls and extract the entire guest database - names, passport numbers, payment tokens and stay histories - through the application's own database connection.

components.name: Hotel Management SaaS Platform
components.description: Cloud-hosted multi-property management platforms serving hundreds of hotel brands from shared infrastructure — a single platform compromise affects every subscribing property simultaneously.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Info-stealer malware on a single hotel employee device harvests SaaS platform credentials stored in the browser - granting attackers cloud-level access to guest records across every property managed through that account.

Multi-tenant SaaS platforms that resolve the caller's property scope from a client-supplied identifier rather than from server-side ownership state allow a compromised account at one property to enumerate and extract guest records from adjacent properties on the same platform.

Vendor-facing integration endpoints that authorise on connector identity alone, without scoping each request to the brands that connector is contracted to serve, allow unauthorised extraction of guest reservation records across multiple hotel brands from a single compromised connector credential.

components.name: Central Reservations System (CRS)
components.description: Platform distributing room availability and booking data across all hotel channels — Amadeus, Sabre SynXis, IHG Concerto. The cross-channel data aggregation point for guest booking histories and personal details.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hard-coded passwords in CRS integration configurations provide a permanent, unrevokable access path to guest booking records and rate configurations distributed across all connected booking channels; because the credential is shared across deployments, rotating it at one property does not close the path.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Overly permissive read access on CRS resources allows users beyond their authorised scope to access guest reservation histories and commercially sensitive rate plans across all distribution channels.

motives.motive: Extract employee PII and loyalty member records in bulk for resale or targeted identity fraud campaigns

components.name: Loyalty Program Platform
components.description: Centralized systems managing guest loyalty accounts, points balances, and member personal information across hotel brands — IHG One Rewards, Marriott Bonvoy, Hilton Honors back-end infrastructure.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Phishing compromise of a single privileged loyalty platform account yields access to millions of member records stored in shared infrastructure - names, email addresses, travel patterns and point balances suitable for targeted fraud campaigns.

Loyalty member queries that are not constrained to the caller's own membership or administrative scope allow any account with a privileged foothold to page through the entire member base - the centralised nature of loyalty platforms means one authorisation failure exposes every member.

components.name: Enterprise HR / ERP System
components.description: Enterprise platforms managing employee payroll, tax records, government IDs, and scheduling across hotel properties — SAP, Oracle HCM, ADP Workforce. Contain the most sensitive employee personal data in the organization.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hospitality organisations running unpatched or end-of-life enterprise HR and ERP platforms expose known, actively exploited CVEs; the window between public disclosure and hotel patching is a reliable route to bulk employee PII. This mapping is retained for its CVE join specifically - it attaches no CAPECs, so the attack patterns for this component come from the permission weakness alongside it.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Overly permissive access to payroll system data allows insider threats or compromised accounts to extract bulk employee PII - Social Security numbers, bank account details and personal addresses - before access controls trigger alerts.

threat: Compromise Guest Accounts to Commit Loyalty and Booking Fraud
threat_description: Adversaries target hotel guest loyalty accounts and booking profiles — using credential stuffing, session hijacking, phishing, and weak password recovery mechanisms — to drain points balances, make unauthorized redemptions, book free stays, and resell stolen credentials in underground markets. Loyalty accounts are particularly attractive: they hold monetary value in redeemable points, require only email and password to access, and are rarely monitored by account holders between stays. The attacker converts a password into a free vacation.

motives.motive: Drain loyalty point balances and book unauthorized free stays using compromised guest accounts

components.name: Guest Authentication Layer
components.description: The login, session management, and identity verification infrastructure for guest-facing hotel applications — web portals, mobile apps, and loyalty member portals. The primary attack surface for account takeover.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Absence of rate limiting on login endpoints allows automated credential stuffing - using lists of breached credentials from other platforms - to systematically test millions of username and password combinations against guest loyalty accounts without triggering lockouts.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Password recovery flows that verify identity through easily obtainable information - email address, booking reference or date of birth - allow attackers to reset guest account credentials and take over loyalty balances without knowing the original password.

Guest loyalty accounts secured by a password alone mean one compromised credential yields complete account access - points, stored payment methods, booking history and profile data - with no second factor to interrupt the takeover.

Session fixation weaknesses allow attackers to pre-establish a known session token and then trick a guest into authenticating with it - giving the attacker a valid authenticated session without ever needing the guest's credentials.

Session tokens that remain valid when replayed from a different client let an attacker who captures one - from an unencrypted channel, a proxy, or via XSS - re-present it and obtain authenticated access for the remainder of the session lifetime, with no binding to the original client to defeat the replay.

components.name: API Gateway
components.description: The API layer routing requests between guest-facing applications and hotel backend services — managing authentication, rate limiting, and access policy enforcement for all programmatic access to guest account functions.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: API credentials exposed in mobile applications or JavaScript bundles allow attackers to make authenticated API calls to guest account endpoints - bypassing the web application's rate limiting and lockout controls that protect the front-end login page.

API endpoints that authorise on the presence of a valid token rather than on the caller's ownership of the requested record allow an authenticated attacker to iterate guest identifiers and read booking records and loyalty balances belonging to other guests.

motives.motive: Harvest and resell compromised loyalty credentials and hotel extranet access in underground markets

components.name: Hotel Extranet and Channel Manager
components.description: Web platforms granting hotel operators access to OTA rate and availability management — Booking.com Extranet, Expedia Partner Central, SiteMinder. Credentials to these systems carry high underground market value for rate manipulation and fraudulent booking attacks.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Extranet credentials harvested through phishing campaigns targeting hotel front desk staff or revenue managers are sold in underground markets - buyers gain the ability to manipulate rate parity, create fraudulent bookings, or redirect guest payments.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirect vulnerabilities in hotel app notification systems allow attackers to craft phishing links that appear to originate from the hotel's own domain - directing loyalty members to credential-harvesting pages that capture usernames and passwords.

threat: Skim Payment Card Data from Hotel POS and Payment Infrastructure
threat_description: Adversaries install memory-scraping malware on hotel point-of-sale terminals, compromise back-office payment systems through remote access, and intercept card data from online ordering platforms — capturing track data, card numbers, and CVVs at the moment of transaction before encryption. Hotel POS environments are high-value targets: a single restaurant or spa terminal processes hundreds of cards per day, back-office systems aggregate data across all outlets, and the distributed nature of hospitality POS infrastructure creates multiple entry points with inconsistent patch management.

motives.motive: Install card-skimming malware on POS infrastructure to harvest bulk payment card data for resale or fraud

components.name: Point of Sale (POS) Terminal
components.description: Physical and software POS terminals processing payment card transactions at hotel restaurants, bars, spas, and retail outlets — Micros, Lightspeed, Toast, NCR Aloha. Card data is present in memory between swipe and encryption.

sub_components.name: Point of Sale Terminal Software and Card Reader Firmware

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: POS terminal memory-scraping malware captures payment card track data in the brief window between card read and encryption - the card number, expiration and service code exist in cleartext in process memory before the encryption module processes them.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: POS software update mechanisms without cryptographic integrity verification allow attackers with network access to push malicious firmware or application updates that install persistent card-scraping malware on every terminal in the property.

components.name: POS Back-Office System
components.description: Server-side infrastructure aggregating transaction data, managing POS terminal configuration, and providing remote administration access across all hotel outlets — the single point of compromise that reaches every payment terminal.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Compromised remote desktop or VPN credentials - often obtained through phishing targeting hotel IT staff - allow attackers to access back-office POS systems and deploy card-scraping malware simultaneously to every terminal managed from that server.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-923: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Back-office POS servers reachable from hotel guest Wi-Fi and general corporate VLANs, rather than restricted to the cardholder data environment, let an attacker who gains any network foothold pivot directly to payment processing infrastructure.

components.name: Online Ordering Platform
components.description: Web and mobile ordering platforms processing payment card data for hotel room service, restaurant pre-orders, and spa bookings — exposed to the internet and subject to web application attacks that terminal-based skimmers cannot reach.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Online ordering checkout pages that load third-party scripts from a CDN or tag manager without integrity pinning execute whatever that origin serves - a compromised dependency silently skims card data entered at checkout, the Magecart pattern applied to hotel ordering infrastructure.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Stored XSS vulnerabilities in online ordering platforms allow attackers to inject persistent card-skimming scripts that silently capture payment details from every subsequent guest who completes an order.

threat: Manipulate Hotel Billing and Payment Systems for Financial Gain
threat_description: Adversaries exploit weak authorization controls, business logic flaws, and insider access in hotel billing, payment, and pricing systems to add fraudulent charges, suppress legitimate ones, divert payments, and manipulate rate configurations. In hospitality, billing is distributed across PMS, POS, event management, and reservations systems — each with its own authorization model. The complexity creates gaps. An insider with access to one system and insufficient audit controls can alter financial records across the entire revenue cycle without detection.

motives.motive: Falsify guest billing records and divert payments for direct financial gain

components.name: Property Management System (PMS)
components.description: The authoritative system of record for guest folios, billing, and charge posting across all hotel departments. PMS billing functions represent the highest-value target for financial manipulation in the hotel ecosystem.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: PMS roles that grant charge posting and financial reconciliation to the same account remove the segregation of duties that would otherwise catch manipulation - an insider or compromised account can both create a fictitious charge and sign off the reconciliation that would have surfaced it.

PMS authorisation models that do not gate folio modification behind an approval workflow allow any authenticated staff account with billing access to alter charge entries without triggering supervisor review or an alert.

components.name: Payment Processing System
components.description: Infrastructure processing and routing payment transactions for hotel services — including refund authorization, discount application, and payment reversal functions that are disproportionately accessible relative to their financial impact.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Payment processing systems that do not enforce dual-control authorisation on high-value refunds and reversals allow a single compromised or malicious account to authorise fraudulent refunds to attacker-controlled payment methods.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Failure to verify the authenticity of pricing data submitted to payment APIs allows tampered or injected values to be accepted as legitimate, enabling unauthorised modification of transaction amounts before settlement.

Missing CSRF protections on web application payment gateway interfaces allow forged requests to manipulate transaction amounts or redirect payment destinations - any authenticated session can be leveraged to submit fraudulent payment modifications.

motives.motive: Exploit insider access to payroll and scheduling systems for unauthorized financial benefit

components.name: Employee Payroll and Scheduling System
components.description: Systems managing employee pay rates, shift assignments, deductions, and direct deposit configurations — ADP, Paychex, Kronos. Insider access to these systems enables financial manipulation that is difficult to detect within normal payroll variance.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Payroll roles that carry rate-change and bank-detail-change rights beyond what the job requires let an attacker modify pay rates, add ghost employees or alter direct deposit routing - manipulation that persists across multiple payroll cycles before anomaly detection triggers a review.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Overly permissive write access on payroll configuration data allows hotel HR or finance staff to make unauthorised changes to compensation records without approval workflows - the modification appears legitimate in audit logs because it originates from an authorised account.

threat_description: Adversaries deploy ransomware across hotel operational technology — property management systems, point-of-sale infrastructure, reservation systems, and cloud management platforms — encrypting the data and systems hotels depend on to check in guests, process payments, and manage properties. The operational dependency is the leverage: a hotel that cannot check in guests generates no revenue from the moment of encryption. Ransomware groups now target hotel management SaaS platforms specifically, achieving simultaneous encryption across hundreds of properties through a single platform compromise.

motives.motive: Encrypt hotel operational systems to extort ransom payment under threat of sustained business disruption

components.name: Property Management System (PMS)
components.description: The operational core of every hotel property — its unavailability prevents guest check-in, room assignment, billing, and keycard issuance. PMS encryption converts the hotel from a functioning operation to a manual fallback overnight.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Compromised employee credentials - obtained through phishing, credential stuffing or infostealer malware - provide ransomware operators with authenticated access to PMS administrative interfaces, from which they deploy encryption payloads across all hotel properties.

Over-privileged PMS service accounts and administrative credentials that span multiple hotel properties allow a single compromised account to provide ransomware operators with the lateral movement path needed to encrypt operations across an entire hotel portfolio.

components.name: Hotel Management SaaS Platform
components.description: Cloud-hosted management platforms serving hundreds of hotel properties from shared infrastructure — a platform-level ransomware deployment simultaneously locks out every subscribing property with no per-property recovery path.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: SaaS administrative interfaces that do not scope destructive operations to a single tenant allow ransomware operators who compromise one platform account to reach every customer environment - one authorisation failure multiplied across every subscribing hotel.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Compromise of a SaaS platform's deployment pipeline or software distribution mechanism allows ransomware operators to distribute malicious updates to all customer environments through the platform's own trusted update channel.

components.name: Point of Sale (POS) System
components.description: Hotel restaurant, bar, and retail POS infrastructure — POS encryption prevents revenue capture across all food and beverage outlets simultaneously, compounding the financial pressure of a hotel-wide ransomware attack.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: POS software update mechanisms without integrity verification allow ransomware operators who gain network access to push malicious payloads to every terminal through the legitimate software update channel - encrypting POS infrastructure across all hotel outlets in a single deployment.

threat: Deceive Hotel Staff into Authorizing Fraudulent Payments
threat_description: Adversaries impersonate trusted parties — OTA platforms like Booking.com, hotel executives, IT vendors, or distressed guests — through phishing emails, AI-cloned voice calls, and spoofed communications to manipulate hotel staff into executing wire transfers, disclosing credentials, or bypassing security procedures. Hospitality staff are trained to help — this social disposition is the attack surface. A front desk agent who would never share a password with an anonymous request will often comply with an urgent request from what appears to be their regional IT support team.

motives.motive: Manipulate hotel finance and operations staff into executing fraudulent wire transfers or payment diversions

components.name: Hotel Staff Email System
components.description: Email infrastructure used by hotel operations, finance, and management staff — the primary delivery channel for business email compromise and spear-phishing attacks targeting hospitality employees.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Mail flow that does not enforce DMARC, DKIM and SPF accepts messages whose stated origin is unverified - letting attackers present as Booking.com, Expedia or the hotel's own executives so that payment instructions arrive inside the trust the staff already extend to that sender.

components.name: Finance and Accounts Payable System
components.description: Financial authorization infrastructure processing vendor payments, wire transfers, and accounts payable — the endpoint targeted by BEC and deepfake fraud after staff trust has been established through initial social engineering.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Payment authorisation that completes on the strength of one channel - an email thread or a phone call - is single-factor by construction: an AI-generated voice impersonating the CFO, or a convincing BEC message from a spoofed executive address, is sufficient to release a wire transfer because no independent out-of-band confirmation is required.

Accounts payable workflows that accept a change of banking details on the authority of the message itself, without verifying the request originated from the supplier of record, allow a spoofed sender to redirect settlement to an attacker-controlled account.

components.name: Help Desk and IT Support
components.description: Internal IT support channels responsible for credential resets and access provisioning — a high-value social engineering target because staff are trained to be helpful and because successful manipulation yields immediate system access.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Help desk credential resets that establish identity from facts an attacker can gather - employee name, property and role - authenticate the caller on knowledge that is not secret, so a vishing call obtains a working reset and immediate authenticated access to hotel management systems.

threat: Deny Hotel Operational Availability Through System Disruption
threat_description: Adversaries flood hotel-facing APIs, booking platforms, management systems, and network infrastructure with malicious traffic or exploitative requests that exhaust processing capacity and deny service to legitimate operations. Unlike ransomware, availability attacks require no persistent access — a sustained request flood against a reservation API prevents bookings for as long as the flood continues, with no encryption or credential needed. IoT-connected hotel systems — smart locks, HVAC, entertainment — expand the disruption surface well beyond traditional IT boundaries.

motives.motive: Exhaust hotel system resources to prevent guest-facing operations and generate financial losses through booking denial

components.name: Reservation and Booking API
components.description: APIs processing guest booking requests, room availability queries, and reservation modifications — the revenue-generating endpoint whose unavailability directly prevents new bookings and check-in processing.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Booking APIs that allocate processing resources per request without per-client throttling allow automated request floods to exhaust server capacity at both the API and the web front end - a sustained attack prevents legitimate guests from completing reservations for as long as it continues.

components.name: IoT Network Infrastructure
components.description: Hotel IoT networks connecting smart locks, HVAC, lighting, entertainment, and access control systems — an increasingly targeted disruption surface where availability attacks affect physical guest experience rather than just digital services.

sub_components.name: Guest-Room IoT and Building Device Network

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-923: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hotel IoT controllers that accept management traffic from any hotel VLAN rather than only from the building automation segment let an attacker with a guest-network foothold reach smart locks, HVAC and in-room entertainment directly and disable them across an entire property.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Unsecured IoT firmware update mechanisms allow attackers to push malicious updates that brick or disable devices across the property - a single malicious update broadcast to all room controllers simultaneously locks guests out of their rooms and requires physical replacement or reflashing to recover.

threat: Endanger Guests by Compromising Hotel Physical Safety Systems
threat_description: Adversaries gain unauthorized access to hotel building management, physical security, and life-safety systems — compromising electronic room locks, disabling fire suppression, manipulating elevator controls, overriding HVAC and pool chemistry, and disabling alarms. The convergence of IT and OT in modern hotels — where the same IP network carries both PMS traffic and BMS commands — means a single network compromise can escalate to physical harm. The attacker does not need physical access to the property to create physical danger inside it.

motives.motive: Gain unauthorized physical access to hotel spaces by subverting electronic lock and access control systems

components.name: Property Management System (PMS)
components.description: The PMS controls room assignments and key encoding — unauthorized PMS access enables creation of master keys, reassignment of occupied rooms, and issuance of access credentials without physical presence at the front desk.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak PMS authentication allows attackers to access room assignment and key issuance functions - an attacker with PMS access can issue valid electronic keys to any room in the property, assign occupied rooms to new guests, or revoke existing keys mid-stay.

Key issuance is authorised by front desk role membership alone, with no separate approval gate between holding a PMS session and encoding a credential for an occupied room - PMS access and physical room access are effectively the same permission.

components.name: Building Management System (BMS)
components.description: Centralized control infrastructure for hotel building systems — HVAC, fire suppression, elevators, lighting, and access control — Honeywell, Siemens Desigo, Johnson Controls Metasys. BMS convergence with IT networks creates a direct path from network compromise to physical system manipulation.

sub_components.name: Building Automation and Life-Safety Control Network

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-923: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: BMS controllers reachable from the same IP network that carries PMS and corporate traffic let any attacker with a hotel IT foothold address fire suppression, elevator and HVAC endpoints directly - IT and OT convergence removes the air gap that previously isolated these safety-critical systems.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Building automation protocols accept control writes on network reachability alone, with no authentication on the operation itself - anything that can address the controller can set HVAC to dangerous extremes, override pool chemical dosing or trigger a false alarm, with no credential required.

motives.motive: Create life-safety hazards for guests and staff by disabling or triggering fire and emergency systems

components.name: Fire Suppression and Safety System
components.description: Networked fire detection, alarm, and suppression infrastructure — Notifier, Simplex, Honeywell fire panels. These systems are increasingly IP-connected for remote monitoring, creating an attack surface that carries direct life-safety consequences.

sub_components.name: Fire Suppression and Emergency Alarm Control Panel

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Weak authentication on building management interfaces allows unauthorised actors to disable fire suppression systems, trigger false alarms that create dangerous evacuation conditions, or prevent genuine alarm activation during a real emergency.

Safety-critical suppression and alarm functions are not restricted to specifically authorised maintenance accounts, so any user holding general building system access can invoke suppression bypass or manual alarm activation without a separate authorisation decision.

threat: Destroy Hotel Operational Records to Sabotage Business Continuity
threat_description: Adversaries exploit weak access controls and insufficient backup verification to delete, corrupt, or irreversibly overwrite hotel reservation records, financial audit trails, loyalty point balances, and employee payroll data. Unlike ransomware — which preserves data under encryption for negotiation leverage — destructive attacks eliminate data entirely. The impact is permanent: a hotel that cannot reconstruct its reservation database cannot fulfill bookings, reconcile revenue, or demonstrate regulatory compliance. The attacker does not need to be present for recovery to fail.

motives.motive: Permanently destroy hotel operational data to prevent business recovery and create maximum financial damage

components.name: Reservation and Property Management Systems
components.description: The authoritative data stores for guest bookings, room assignments, and operational records — their destruction prevents the hotel from fulfilling existing reservations, reconciling revenue, and demonstrating service delivery to guests and regulators.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Operational reservation roles carry destructive rights - bulk delete and purge - that the day-to-day job never needs, so an account compromised for read access is already sufficient to destroy the records it could previously only query.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Overly permissive write and delete permissions on critical operational data stores allow insider threats or compromised accounts to destroy audit trails - eliminating the evidence of both the attack and any prior fraudulent activity the attacker sought to conceal.

Absence of CSRF protections on reservation management endpoints allows forged cross-site requests to modify or cancel bookings on behalf of authenticated staff and guests - an attacker can systematically destroy reservation records without ever holding a credential.

components.name: Loyalty Program Platform
components.description: Guest loyalty point balances and member account histories — destruction of loyalty data eliminates the financial liability represented by outstanding point balances while simultaneously destroying the member relationship that represents long-term brand value.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-472: External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Loyalty update APIs that accept point balances, tier status and member identifiers from the request body and treat them as authoritative let an attacker overwrite balances, corrupt member profiles and trigger cascading deletions across linked account records by editing values the server should have owned.

threat: Weaponize Hotel Infrastructure to Damage Brand Reputation
threat_description: Adversaries exploit vulnerabilities in hotel web applications, IoT devices, Kubernetes clusters, and guest-facing platforms to distribute malware, redirect guests to phishing sites, and execute infrastructure abuse that triggers public incident disclosure, regulatory enforcement action, and media coverage. In hospitality, brand trust is the product — guests choose hotels because they trust them with their safety, data, and payment credentials. A single publicized breach of that trust generates reputational damage that outlasts the technical incident by years.

motives.motive: Exploit hotel infrastructure to distribute malware and phishing content to guests, triggering public trust damage

components.name: Hotel Web Application
components.description: Guest-facing hotel websites and booking portals — the public face of the hotel brand and the platform through which attackers can distribute malicious content to the hotel's own guests at scale.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Stored XSS vulnerabilities in hotel web application user-generated content - reviews, profile fields, booking comments - allow attackers to inject persistent malicious scripts that execute in every guest's browser who visits the affected page, distributing malware through the hotel's own trusted domain.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open redirect vulnerabilities in hotel booking confirmation and communication flows allow attackers to craft URLs on the hotel's own domain that redirect guests to phishing sites - the hotel's trusted domain name becomes the attack delivery mechanism.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hotel web application download sections or software distribution endpoints without integrity verification allow attackers to substitute legitimate files with malware-laden versions - guests who download hotel apps or tools from the official site receive attacker-controlled code.

components.name: Kubernetes Cluster
components.description: Container orchestration infrastructure running hotel application workloads — cluster compromise provides the compute resources and outbound network access needed to conduct large-scale attacks that are attributed to the hotel's infrastructure.

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Misconfigured Kubernetes workloads running with host-level or cluster-admin privileges allow container escapes that give attackers control over the underlying host - providing infrastructure for external attacks, spam campaigns or cryptomining that generate abuse reports traced back to the hotel's IP ranges.

Deserialization vulnerabilities in Kubernetes-hosted hotel application components allow attackers to execute arbitrary code within the cluster and establish persistence - using hotel compute and network resources for external attacks that produce regulatory notifications and public attribution.

threat: Compromise Hotel Technology Suppliers to Reach Guest Data at Scale
threat_description: Adversaries target the vendors, integrators and managed service providers that hotels depend on rather than the hotels themselves - property management vendors, channel managers, payment connectors, loyalty platforms and the outsourced IT firms that hold remote access to hundreds of properties. Hospitality is unusually exposed here: a mid-sized operator typically runs no software it wrote, integrates dozens of third-party connectors, and grants standing remote access to vendors for support. One compromised update channel or connector credential reaches every property on the platform at once, and the hotel has no visibility into the vendor's own security posture.

motives.motive: Compromise a hospitality platform vendor to reach every property running that platform through a single trusted channel

components.name: PMS and CRS Vendor Update Channel

sub_components.name: Vendor Software Update and Patch Distribution

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hotel management software distributed through an update channel that does not verify package integrity before installation lets an attacker who reaches the distribution point replace a legitimate release - every property that applies the update installs attacker-controlled code as a routine maintenance task.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Update packages whose signatures are absent, unchecked, or validated against a key the installer will accept without pinning give a compromised or impersonated vendor a path onto every property's servers; the hotel has no independent means of telling a genuine release from a forged one.

Connector credentials for channel managers, loyalty platforms and payment gateways are commonly stored in plaintext configuration on the vendor side and shared across the vendor's whole customer base - recovering one set yields authenticated access to every hotel that vendor serves.

Integration endpoints that authorise on connector identity alone, without constraining each call to the properties that connector is contracted to serve, let a single compromised partner read reservation and guest data far beyond its commercial scope.

components.name: Hotel Software Build and Release Pipeline

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Build pipelines that resolve dependencies from public registries at build time, without pinning or checksum verification, incorporate whatever those registries serve at that moment - a typosquatted or hijacked package is compiled into the hotel's own booking and loyalty applications.

Code committed or injected into the release pipeline ships to production under the hotel's own signing identity and reputation, so a payload planted once executes in every property's environment with the trust granted to first-party software.

motives.motive: Abuse vendor and managed service provider remote access to move laterally into hotel estates

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Standing vendor support accounts protected by a shared password alone, often reused across the vendor's customers and rarely rotated after staff turnover, give an attacker who obtains one credential direct authenticated entry into hotel systems with no second factor to interrupt it.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-923: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Vendor remote access that terminates on the flat hotel network rather than on a bastion scoped to the supported application lets a compromised support session reach payment, property management and building systems that the vendor was never engaged to touch.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hotels that cannot enumerate the third-party components inside their booking, loyalty and payment stacks cannot tell which properties are exposed when a vendor discloses a vulnerability, so known-exploited CVEs stay unpatched for months. This mapping is retained for its CVE join specifically - it attaches no CAPECs, so the attack patterns for this component come from the dependency weakness alongside it.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-829: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Hotel applications that load functionality from vendor-hosted scripts, SDKs and tag managers at runtime execute whatever those origins serve - the hotel inherits the security of every supplier in that chain without any deployment step of its own.

threat: Intercept Guest Communications on Hotel Network Infrastructure
threat_description: Adversaries exploit the shared, low-friction wireless networks hotels provide to capture guest credentials, session tokens and personal data in transit, and to pivot from the guest network into corporate and payment systems. Hotel Wi-Fi is deliberately easy to join - a room number and surname, or nothing at all - and guests connect corporate laptops and phones to it while travelling, often to reach employer systems. The attacker needs only to book a room. Rogue access points, captive portal manipulation and weak isolation between guest, staff and building networks turn a hospitality amenity into a position on the network.

motives.motive: Capture guest credentials, sessions and personal data from shared hotel wireless networks

sub_components.name: Guest Wi-Fi Access Points and Wireless LAN Controller

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Open or PSK-shared guest wireless carries traffic that is not encrypted between client and access point, so every other guest on the same SSID can read unencrypted sessions, tokens and credentials in transit - the shared key is printed on the welcome card and is not a confidentiality boundary.

Guest wireless clients cannot distinguish the hotel's access points from an attacker's, so a rogue AP advertising the same SSID from a guest room places the attacker between every associating device and the network, reading and modifying traffic for the duration of the stay.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Captive portals that collect room number, surname and loyalty number over an unencrypted pre-authentication channel expose exactly the identifiers needed to impersonate a guest at the front desk or in the loyalty programme, to anyone already listening on the same wireless segment.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Captive portal redirect parameters that accept an arbitrary destination let an attacker publish a link that traverses the hotel's own portal domain before landing on a credential harvesting page, borrowing the trust guests extend to the network they just paid to join.

sub_components.name: Hotel VLAN Segmentation and Wireless Client Isolation

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-923: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Guest wireless that shares layer 2 or routes freely to staff, property management and payment segments converts any guest device into a foothold on the hotel's internal network - the room rate is the cost of network access.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Internal hotel services reachable from the guest segment that authenticate on network position rather than on a credential - printers, file shares, building controllers, management consoles - are open to anyone who associates with the guest SSID.

motives.motive: Pivot from the guest wireless network into hotel corporate and payment systems

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Wireless controllers left on vendor default or single-factor administrative credentials, reachable from the same networks they serve, hand an attacker control of every access point in the property from a single login.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-15: External Control of System or Configuration Setting
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Controller settings that can be changed without an approval or integrity check - VLAN assignment, isolation, captive portal target, RADIUS destination - let an attacker who reaches the console re-point guest traffic or dissolve the segmentation that separates guests from payment systems.

sub_components.name: Guest-Room Media, Casting and Set-Top Devices

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: In-room casting and entertainment systems identify guests by room number or by the device already on the room VLAN, so an attacker who spoofs that identifier can address another guest's screen - displaying content, capturing casting sessions, or reading the folio data the system surfaces.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Set-top and casting endpoints expose control and diagnostic functions to anything that can reach them on the room network, with no authentication on the operation itself - an attacker in one room reaches the devices in every other.

threat: Subvert Electronic Room Access and Key Management
threat_description: Adversaries forge, clone or replay the electronic credentials that open hotel guest rooms, and compromise the systems that issue and audit them. Hotel locks are a distinctive target: they are battery-powered, offline for long periods, deployed in the thousands per property, and expected to last a decade, so cryptography and firmware age in place while the attacker's tools improve. The consequence is not data loss but physical entry to occupied rooms, and an audit trail the attacker can often edit afterwards - which makes both guest safety incidents and liability disputes turn on records the intruder controlled.

motives.motive: Forge, clone or replay electronic room credentials to gain unauthorised physical entry

sub_components.name: Guest-Room Lock Firmware and Onboard Credential Store

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Offline door locks validate a credential presented at the door without any freshness or challenge step, so a credential captured from a card or a mobile handset can be replayed against that lock later - the lock cannot tell a live presentation from a recorded one.

Locks that accept any credential carrying the right room and property identifiers, without verifying it was issued by the property's own encoder, allow a forged or cloned card to open the door as the legitimate guest key.

components.name: Key Encoder and Credential Issuance Terminal

sub_components.name: Front Desk Key Encoder and Blank Card Stock

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Front desk encoders that will write a working room credential for anyone with physical access to the terminal, with no operator authentication on the encode operation itself, turn a moment of unattended reception into a key for any room in the property.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Encoders that accept the room assignment supplied to them without verifying it against current reservation state will issue a valid credential for a room the requester has no claim to, including rooms that are presently occupied.

Mobile room keys stored in application storage or a device keychain without hardware backing can be extracted from a rooted, stolen or malware-bearing handset and re-used against the lock, with no physical card for the property to collect at checkout.
Mobile key handoff over Bluetooth that carries no per-unlock challenge lets an attacker within radio range record an unlock exchange and replay it at the same door afterwards.

motives.motive: Compromise the lock management server to issue, revoke or erase room credentials at scale

cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Lock management platforms that gate credential issuance on staff role alone, with no separate authorisation for master and emergency credentials, let any compromised front desk account mint keys that open every door in the property.

Maintenance and vendor accounts on lock management servers routinely carry master-key and audit-clearing rights they do not need for routine work, so compromising the lowest-privileged support account is sufficient to reach every room and remove the evidence.

components.name: Lock Audit Trail and Access Log

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Access logs writable by the same accounts that issue credentials allow an intruder to delete the record of their own entry - the property then cannot establish who opened a door during a guest safety incident or a theft claim.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Audit purge and log rotation functions exposed without authentication on the operation let anyone who reaches the management interface clear the trail wholesale rather than editing individual entries.
